low_hemoglobin.title: Low hemoglobin
low_hemoglobin.summary: Hemoglobin below the lab reference range can relate to anemia. Common educational themes include fatigue, reduced exercise tolerance, and the need to identify underlying causes with a clinician.
risks: Persistent low hemoglobin may be associated with iron deficiency or other causes of anemia
Symptoms can include tiredness, shortness of breath on exertion, and pale skin
remedies: Discuss results with a clinician before starting supplements
A balanced diet with iron-rich foods may be discussed when appropriate
Follow-up labs are often used to track trends

microcytic_pattern.title: Low MCV with low MCH
microcytic_pattern.summary: When mean corpuscular volume (MCV) and mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH) are both low, labs often describe a microcytic pattern. Iron deficiency is a commonly discussed educational association, but only a clinician can interpret an individual case.
risks: Microcytic patterns are frequently discussed in the context of iron deficiency
Ongoing patterns may prompt further evaluation of diet, blood loss, or other causes
remedies: Share CBC trends with a clinician
Do not self-start high-dose iron without medical advice
Ask whether ferritin or iron studies are appropriate

high_neutrophils.title: Elevated neutrophil percentage
high_neutrophils.summary: A high neutrophil percentage on a CBC differential can occur with infection, inflammation, stress, or other contexts. It is a lab pattern, not a diagnosis by itself.
risks: Marked or persistent neutrophilia may warrant clinical correlation with symptoms
Isolated percentage shifts should be interpreted with absolute counts and clinical history
remedies: Note any fever, recent illness, or medications when talking to a clinician
Repeat testing may be suggested if the result is unexpected

high_blood_sugar.title: Elevated blood sugar
high_blood_sugar.summary: Higher-than-reference glucose values are discussed in relation to diabetes risk and metabolic health. Long-term elevation is associated in educational materials with eye, kidney, and heart complications — interpretation belongs with a clinician.
risks: Sustained high blood sugar is linked in public health materials to complications affecting eyes, kidneys, and heart
Single abnormal values need clinical context and often confirmation
remedies: Discuss diet, activity, and follow-up testing with a clinician
Do not change prescribed diabetes medicines based on an app insight

hiv_1_2_abnormal.title: Reactive HIV screening result
hiv_1_2_abnormal.summary: A reactive HIV-1/2 screening test is not a final diagnosis. Public health guidance emphasizes confirmatory testing and prompt clinical follow-up.
risks: Screening tests can be falsely reactive; confirmation is required
Delayed follow-up can postpone care if infection is confirmed
remedies: Contact a clinician or testing program promptly for confirmatory testing
Use official public health resources for next-step guidance

hcv_antibody_abnormal.title: Reactive HCV antibody
hcv_antibody_abnormal.summary: A reactive hepatitis C antibody test indicates exposure and needs RNA/confirmatory testing to determine current infection status.
risks: Antibody positivity alone does not confirm active infection
Untreated chronic HCV can affect liver health over time
remedies: Ask a clinician about HCV RNA testing and linkage to care
Avoid interpreting antibody results as a standalone diagnosis

hbsag_abnormal.title: Reactive HBsAg
hbsag_abnormal.summary: Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) reactivity suggests current hepatitis B infection and requires clinical evaluation and further serology.
risks: Chronic hepatitis B can affect long-term liver health
Household and partner counseling may be clinically relevant
remedies: Seek clinician follow-up for confirmatory panels and care planning
Do not rely on an app for diagnosis or treatment decisions
